mods.name: Nimbus
mods.description: All-in-one optimization for client and server: its own terrain renderer (GPU culling, occlusion culling, instanced entities and particles, distant LOD), a shader pack loader that works without Iris, Lithium-style server optimizations, lower memory use and faster loading. Replaces Sodium, Lithium, FerriteCore, ModernFix, ImmediatelyFast and more; changes nothing visible by default.

releases.notes:
Final release of the 4.0 line.

- Hi-Z occlusion culling on by default, combined with GPU frustum culling; it pauses itself in open views where it would not pay off (+30% FPS in occluded scenes).
- Smooth chunk fade-in (optional).
- Dynamic lights: torches and lanterns in hand, dropped light sources, burning mobs (optional; steps aside for LambDynamicLights).
- "Pick for my hardware" button for graphics profiles.
- Server: faster scheduled ticks, cached piston shapes, cheaper explosion exposure; entity fluid checks no longer wait for chunk generation.
- About 30 MB less heap.
- Async screenshots, precise frame limiter, frame-time graph, anisotropic filtering, Iris-style shader keys, new settings screen and a dedicated shader screen.

Requires Minecraft 1.21.1, Fabric Loader 0.16+, Fabric API, Java 21.

releases.notes:
Client:

- Fast world quit: leaving a singleplayer world returns to the menu in about 0.1 s instead of 3–6 s, while the world saves in the background.
  - Opening that world again waits for the save to finish, and so does closing the game.
  - Option: Interface → Fast world quit. Turned off when the FastQuit mod is installed.
- Nether: about 750 → about 1000 FPS in the test scene, level with Sodium.
  - LOD is off in dimensions with a roof (its height map there is just the bedrock ceiling).
  - Repairing dark light spots no longer re-checks sections whose light data did not change.
- Without Sodium, transparent texture pixels are filled with a darkened average colour before mipmaps are built: fast leaves no longer show black holes, and mipmaps lose their dark fringes.
- Memory: about 30 MB less heap in a 16-chunk world.
  - One shared threading detector instead of a detector, semaphore and lock per chunk palette (`paletteLocks`).
  - Palette configurations are interned.
  - Multipart model predicates are shared (`dedupModels`, unless FerriteCore is installed).
  - Vanilla section buffers create their GL buffers and vertex arrays only on first use. With the Nimbus engine they are never used, so the driver keeps about 390 000 fewer objects.

Checked with the non-performance mods of a typical optimized pack in place of Sodium, Lithium, FerriteCore, ModernFix, ImmediatelyFast, EntityCulling, MoreCulling, Dynamic FPS, EBE and FastQuit.

releases.notes:
Server (and integrated server):

- Every grounded entity looks for the block under its feet and "falls" 0.08 into the ground on each tick, standing still included. Both results are now kept per entity while its box, the move and the blocks around are the same and the blocks' collision shapes depend on the block state alone (water, powder snow, scaffolding and moving pistons always recompute). Self-check with `-Dnimbus.verifySupport=true` compares every reuse with a fresh vanilla computation: over a million reuses, no difference.
- Mob AI scene (200 villagers with beds and job sites, 300 animals, 160 monsters): 11.0 → 8.6 ms per tick. Lithium: 12.6, vanilla: 18.5.
- Switches in `config/nimbus-common.properties`: `supportCache`, `fallCache`. Checks against vanilla still pass bit for bit (hoppers, TNT, collisions, moves, POI, section packing).
